claims: C1 the assistant should seek clarification when an instruction might be intended
C2 the duty to seek clarification applies when carrying out that instruction could cause serious side effects
C3 the duty is triggered by the possibility, not the certainty, that the instruction was intended and that side effects would be serious

concepts.name: root_authority
concepts.gloss: the rule carries root authority, the highest level of the chain of command, as established by the #ignore_untrusted_data section

concepts.name: instruction_might_be_intended
concepts.gloss: I is an instruction that might have been intended by the user, even if not certain
concepts.inference: the clause says 'might be intended', so the trigger is a possibility rather than a certainty; whether a given instruction is possibly intended is a fact about the case

concepts.name: serious_side_effects
concepts.gloss: carrying out I could cause serious side effects, such as significant harm or irreversible consequences
concepts.inference: the clause refers to 'serious side effects' without defining them; what counts as serious is a fact about the case

concepts.name: tool_instruction
concepts.gloss: I is an instruction that would be carried out through a tool, as opposed to a direct assistant response
concepts.inference: the clause speaks of 'tool instructions', so the instruction must be one that operates through a tool

asserts.read_back: the assistant should seek clarification about instruction % when it might be intended and carrying it out could cause serious side effects

closure.reason: the clause obliges seeking clarification only when an instruction might be intended and could cause serious side effects; it does not forbid seeking clarification in other cases, so silence permits it
